articles.title: Hong Kong Food Stalls Reminded: Plastic-Lined Bowls Not Allowed for Dine-In Meals
articles.summary: Hong Kong's Environmental Protection Department has reminded restaurant owners that paper bowls and containers with a plastic coating on the inside cannot be used when customers eat inside a restaurant or food court. Officers visited food stalls at a shopping centre in Sham Shui Po on July 23 and handed out warnings to multiple operators. Some stall owners said they were surprised because they did not realise their bowls broke the city's single-use plastics rules, which first came into force in April 2024. The department explained that plastic-lined paper products may only be used for takeaway orders, not for dine-in service. Switching to fully approved containers will cost some businesses extra money.

lv1: What kind of containers are food stalls NOT allowed to use when customers eat inside? (食客在餐廳堂食時，食物攤檔不可使用哪種容器？)
Which government department sent officers to check the food stalls? (哪個政府部門派人到食物攤檔巡查？)
lv2: Why do you think some food stall owners did not know their containers were breaking the law? (你認為為什麼部分食物攤檔東主不知道他們的容器違規？)
What is the difference between rules for dine-in service and takeaway orders under Hong Kong's plastics ban? (根據香港的膠樽禁令，堂食和外賣的規定有何分別？)
lv3: Should the government give businesses more time and support before enforcing new environmental rules, or should strict penalties apply from day one? Explain your view. (政府在執行新環保規例前，應給予商戶更多時間和支援，還是應從第一天起嚴格執法？請解釋你的立場。)

Some people say banning plastics is important for the environment, but others worry it makes things harder and more expensive for small businesses. Who do you think is right, and why? (有人認為禁用塑膠對環境很重要，但也有人擔心這會增加小商戶的困難和成本。你認為誰的看法更有道理？為什麼？)

articles.title: Hong Kong Leader Praises First Lawmakers Meeting, Officials Say Big Events Help the Economy
articles.summary: Hong Kong's Chief Executive John Lee described his first policy exchange session with members of the Legislative Council as a warm and productive experience. The meeting gave government officials and lawmakers a chance to discuss policy ideas directly. Separately, a senior official said that large-scale events hosted in Hong Kong, such as concerts, sports competitions, and international festivals, can encourage both locals and visitors to spend more money in the city. Hong Kong has been actively attracting major events as part of a plan to boost tourism and strengthen the economy. Authorities believe these gatherings can create jobs and increase business for restaurants, shops, and hotels across the city.

lv1: What did Chief Executive John Lee think of his first meeting with lawmakers? (行政長官李家超對首次與立法會議員的政策交流會有何感受？)
How can large events held in Hong Kong help local businesses? (在香港舉辦的大型活動如何幫助本地商戶？)
lv2: Why is it helpful for a city's leader to meet regularly with lawmakers? (為什麼一個城市的領導人定期與立法會議員會面是有益的？)
Besides entertainment, what other benefits can international events bring to a city like Hong Kong? (除了娛樂之外，國際大型活動還能為香港這樣的城市帶來什麼其他好處？)
lv3: Some people argue that hosting mega events mainly benefits tourists and wealthy businesses, while ordinary residents see little gain. Do you agree? Give reasons from different perspectives. (有人認為舉辦大型活動主要惠及遊客和大企業，普通市民所獲甚少。你同意嗎？請從不同角度說明理由。)

Should government leaders prioritise regular dialogue with lawmakers, or focus more on consulting the general public and civil society? What are the strengths and weaknesses of each approach? (政府領導人應優先與立法會議員定期對話，還是更多諮詢普通市民及公民社會？各有什麼優缺點？)

articles.title: 青衣城父子因家事爭執持鋸互鬥　警方拘捕兩人
articles.summary: 青衣城商場早前發生一宗因家庭糾紛引發的暴力事件。一名78歲父親與52歲兒子因家事起爭執，在人多的商場內大打出手，父親更取出鋸刀追逐兒子，令附近市民十分驚慌。警方接報後到場調查，以「在公眾地方打鬥」及「藏有攻擊性武器」兩項罪名將父子二人逮捕，並檢走鋸刀等證物。事件反映家庭矛盾若處理不當，可能演變成危及公眾安全的暴力行為，提醒市民應以理性和平方式化解家庭衝突。

lv1: 事件中父親用了什麼物品追逐兒子？
警方以哪兩項罪名逮捕了父子二人？
lv2: 為什麼在公眾場所藏有攻擊性武器是嚴重的罪行？
面對家庭爭執，你認為有哪些比暴力更好的解決方法？
lv3: 社會應提供哪些支援服務，幫助家庭在衝突升級為暴力之前解決問題？這些服務應由誰負責提供？
有觀點認為執法人員處理家庭糾紛時應更具彈性，也有觀點認為法律應對所有人一視同仁。你認同哪個立場，為什麼？

articles.title: 消息指今年《施政報告》或提前九月發表　官方未有確認時間表
articles.summary: 據悉，香港特區政府今年的《施政報告》發表日期尚未最終落實，有消息指當局正考慮將報告提前至九月公布，較以往在十月發表提早約一個月。《施政報告》是行政長官每年向市民交代政府施政方向及新政策的重要文件，內容涵蓋教育、房屋、經濟及民生各方面。若時間表提前，政府可更早推行各項措施，惟各界提交意見的時間亦會相應縮短。目前政府未就具體日期作出正式公告。

lv1: 《施政報告》通常在哪個月份發表？
《施政報告》涵蓋哪些重要的民生範疇？
lv2: 如果《施政報告》提前發表，對市民參與諮詢會有什麼影響？
為什麼《施政報告》對香港市民的日常生活十分重要？
lv3: 你認為政府制定政策時，應更多依靠市民意見，還是主要由官員和專家主導決策？試從不同立場分析兩種做法的優劣。
有人認為提早發表《施政報告》可加快推行政策，有人則擔心諮詢時間不足令政策質素下降。你認為哪個考慮更為重要？請提出理由。
